_comment: Who a province can raise in its yard. Engine data, not a campaign's. 'cost' is what ONE man needs — people out of the province's population, and the weapon the smithy forged for him, out of its armoury — so an intake of ten costs ten of each. 'batch' is how many the captain is asked for to begin with. Men are raised the turn they are paid for, so there is no drill time to give. The four stats are 0..10 bars, and they are what a battle is decided by as well as what the card shows. 'mounted' is the one thing a man cannot take up a ladder: horses win a field and are worth nothing against a wall. Every number here is placeholder balance, meant to be tuned.

items.name: Peasant
items.blurb: Farmhands with whatever hangs in the barn. They cost nothing but the hands that were working the fields.
items.strengths: Good for: numbers, and they cost no weapon. Weak in every fight, and every one raised is a hand off the fields.

items.name: Spearmen
items.blurb: The line that holds. Cheap to raise and quick to drill, and a wall of points is what a charge breaks on.
items.strengths: Good for: holding a line — the best defence the yard raises. Slow on the field, and short of a killing blow.

items.name: Archers
items.blurb: Months of drawing before a man is worth his bow, but he thins a charge long before it reaches the line.
items.strengths: Good for: killing at a distance before the lines meet, and quick on their feet. Cut down if anyone reaches them.

items.name: Crossbowmen
items.blurb: Anyone can be taught to aim one in a fortnight, which is the whole point of the weapon.
items.strengths: Good for: the hardest blow of any shooter. The slowest men on the field, and poor once the enemy is close.

items.name: Swordsmen
items.blurb: Disciplined infantry, and the men a lord puts where the fighting is decided.
items.strengths: Good for: the melee — hit hard and hard to kill, at a fair pace. Nothing to shoot with.

items.name: Macemen
items.blurb: Heavy, crude and indifferent to armour. What you raise when the enemy comes in plate.
items.strengths: Good for: hitting hard up close. Lighter armour than the swordsmen and slower on the field.

items.name: Cavalry
items.blurb: The costliest men a province can raise, and the only ones who decide a field in a single charge.
items.strengths: Good for: the hardest charge and the fastest legs on the field — horses outrun every man on foot. No use at an assault: a horse cannot climb a wall. Two people each.
